review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Συνίστημι δὲ ὑμῖν Φοίβην τὴν ἀδελφὴν ἡμῶν, οὖσαν διάκονον τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἐν Κενχρεαῖς,
16:1.targetText: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the participle οὖσαν ("being") untranslated; a servant stands in apposition to Phoebe.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:2.sourceText: ἵνα αὐτὴν προσδέξησθε ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀξίως τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ παραστῆτε αὐτῇ ἐν ᾧ ἂν ὑμῶν χρῄζῃ πράγματι· καὶ γὰρ αὐτὴ προστάτις πολλῶν ἐγενήθη καὶ ἐμοῦ αὐτοῦ.
16:2.targetText: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

groups.note: The adverb ἀξίως ("worthily") is rendered in a manner worthy.
ἐν ᾧ ἂν … πράγματι ("in whatever matter") is rendered with anything.
καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns the ἵνα ("so that") clause into the command Welcome; ἵνα has no English word.
BSB leaves the intensive αὐτοῦ ("myself") untranslated.

16:3.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν τοὺς συνεργούς μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
16:3.targetText: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:4.sourceText: οἵτινες ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς μου τὸν ἑαυτῶν τράχηλον ὑπέθηκαν, οἷς οὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος εὐχαριστῶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσαι αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῶν ἐθνῶν,
16:4.targetText: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.

groups.note: ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς μου ("for my life") is rendered for me.
In the idiom "lay down the neck", τράχηλον ("neck") is rendered lives.
The relative οἷς ("to whom") is rendered to them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB has no word for καί ("also") after but.

16:5.sourceText: καὶ τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίαν. ἀσπάσασθε Ἐπαίνετον τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου, ὅς ἐστιν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀσίας εἰς Χριστόν.
16:5.targetText: Greet also the church that meets at their house.  Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.

groups.note: ἀπαρχή ("firstfruits") is rendered the first convert.
The genitive Ἀσίας ("of Asia") is rendered in … Asia.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB repeats Greet from verse 3; the Greek continues that sentence with καί.
English supplies a relative clause for κατ’ οἶκον ("at the house").
BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.

16:6.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Μαριάν, ἥτις πολλὰ ἐκοπίασεν εἰς ὑμᾶς.
16:6.targetText: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.

16:7.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ἀνδρόνικον καὶ Ἰουνίαν τοὺς συγγενεῖς μου καὶ συναιχμαλώτους μου, οἵτινές εἰσιν ἐπίσημοι ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις, οἳ καὶ πρὸ ἐμοῦ γέγοναν ἐν Χριστῷ.
16:7.targetText: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.

groups.note: γέγοναν ("they have been") is understood again in before I was.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB says my only once, for both nouns.

16:8.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ἀμπλιᾶτον τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου ἐν Κυρίῳ.
16:8.targetText: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:9.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Οὐρβανὸν τὸν συνεργὸν ἡμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ Στάχυν τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου.
16:9.targetText: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:10.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ἀπελλῆν τὸν δόκιμον ἐν Χριστῷ. ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐκ τῶν Ἀριστοβούλου.
16:10.targetText: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ.  Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.

groups.note: The article τόν is rendered who.
The article τούς is used as a pronoun ("those").
ἐκ ("from, of") is rendered belong to.
The article τῶν with the genitive name stands for his household ("those of Aristobulus").

16:11.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ἡρῳδίωνα τὸν συγγενῆ μου. ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐκ τῶν Ναρκίσσου τοὺς ὄντας ἐν Κυρίῳ.
16:11.targetText: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman.  Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

groups.note: The article τούς is used as a pronoun ("those").
The article τῶν with the genitive name stands for his household ("those of Narcissus").
The article with the participle ὄντας ("being") is rendered who are.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:12.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Τρύφαιναν καὶ Τρυφῶσαν τὰς κοπιώσας ἐν Κυρίῳ. ἀσπάσασθε Περσίδα τὴν ἀγαπητήν, ἥτις πολλὰ ἐκοπίασεν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
16:12.targetText: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord.  Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.

groups.note: The feminine article with the participle κοπιώσας ("laboring") is rendered women who have worked hard.

16:13.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ῥοῦφον τὸν ἐκλεκτὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμοῦ.
16:13.targetText: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.

groups.note: μητέρα ("mother") is stated once; BSB repeats it for "and mine".
ἐμοῦ ("of me, mine") is rendered to me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for "and mine".

16:14.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Ἀσύνκριτον, Φλέγοντα, Ἑρμῆν, Πατρόβαν, Ἑρμᾶν, καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς ἀδελφούς.
16:14.targetText: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

16:15.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε Φιλόλογον καὶ Ἰουλίαν, Νηρέα καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ὀλυμπᾶν, καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς πάντας ἁγίους.
16:15.targetText: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:16.sourceText: ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι πᾶσαι τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
16:16.targetText: Greet one another with a holy kiss.  All the churches of Christ send you greetings.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:17.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, σκοπεῖν τοὺς τὰς διχοστασίας καὶ τὰ σκάνδαλα παρὰ τὴν διδαχὴν ἣν ὑμεῖς ἐμάθετε ποιοῦντας, καὶ ἐκκλίνετε ἀπ’ αὐτῶν·
16:17.targetText: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.

groups.note: The article τούς with the participle ποιοῦντας ("making") is rendered those who create.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative ἥν ("which") unexpressed.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause with a copula.

16:18.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Χριστῷ οὐ δουλεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τῇ ἑαυτῶν κοιλίᾳ, καὶ διὰ τῆς χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐλογίας ἐξαπατῶσιν τὰς καρδίας τῶν ἀκάκων.
16:18.targetText: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.

groups.note: κοιλίᾳ ("belly") is rendered appetites.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί untranslated.

16:19.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ ὑμῶν ὑπακοὴ εἰς πάντας ἀφίκετο· ἐφ’ ὑμῖν οὖν χαίρω, θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς σοφοὺς εἶναι εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν, ἀκεραίους δὲ εἰς τὸ κακόν.
16:19.targetText: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

groups.note: πάντας ("all") becomes the subject Everyone.
ἀφίκετο ("reached") is told from the other side: "your obedience has reached all" becomes Everyone has heard about your obedience.
The article τό makes ἀγαθόν ("good") a noun, rendered what is good.
The article τό makes κακόν ("evil") a noun, rendered what is evil.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ ("for") untranslated.
BSB makes πάντας the subject Everyone, so εἰς ("to") has no separate word.

16:20.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης συντρίψει τὸν Σατανᾶν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ὑμῶν ἐν τάχει. Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
16:20.targetText: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

groups.note: ἐν τάχει ("in quickness") is rendered soon.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

16:21.sourceText: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Τιμόθεος ὁ συνεργός μου, καὶ Λούκιος καὶ Ἰάσων καὶ Σωσίπατρος οἱ συγγενεῖς μου.
16:21.targetText: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.

groups.note: BSB resumes ἀσπάζεται ("greets") with do for the other names.
καί ("and") is rendered as.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
καί ("and") between Lucius and Jason is shown by a comma in English.

16:22.sourceText: ἀσπάζομαι ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ Τέρτιος ὁ γράψας τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
16:22.targetText: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.

groups.note: The article with the participle γράψας ("having written") is rendered who wrote down.

16:23.sourceText: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Γάϊος ὁ ξένος μου καὶ ὅλης τῆς ἐκκλησίας. ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἔραστος ὁ οἰκονόμος τῆς πόλεως καὶ Κούαρτος ὁ ἀδελφός.
16:23.targetText: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings.  Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.

groups.note: The noun ξένος ("host") is rendered as a verb, has hosted.
BSB resumes ἀσπάζεται ("greets") with does for Quartus.
καί ("and") is rendered as.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:25.sourceText: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ ὑμᾶς στηρίξαι κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν μυστηρίου χρόνοις αἰωνίοις σεσιγημένου,
16:25.targetText: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past

groups.note: The article with the participle δυναμένῳ ("being able") is rendered to Him who is able.
κατά governs both nouns; BSB repeats by.
χρόνοις αἰωνίοις ("for eternal times") is rendered for ages past.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:26.sourceText: φανερωθέντος δὲ νῦν διά τε γραφῶν προφητικῶν κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ αἰωνίου Θεοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη γνωρισθέντος,
16:26.targetText: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith—

groups.note: τε links the participles revealed and made known.
The adjective προφητικῶν ("prophetic") is rendered of the prophets.
The genitive πίστεως ("of faith") is rendered from faith.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes all nations the object of lead, so εἰς ("to") has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the purpose phrase; the Greek has no word for lead.
English supplies a relative frame for the genitive.

16:27.sourceText: μόνῳ σοφῷ Θεῷ, διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
16:27.targetText: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.

groups.note: εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ("to the ages of the ages") is rendered forever.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for the relative ᾧ ("to whom"), which refers back to God.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
